digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate judge reliability measurement (Pass-2 verify / Pass-3 decide)
key_entities: decision enum: block, advisory, dropped, indeterminate
propositions: The LLM judge in the plan-review gate exhibits self-consistency drift across repeated Pass-2/Pass-3 decision cycles; E6 measures Fleiss' κ and raw agreement on 50 re-judged G6/E4/T3 findings over 3 votes each to verify κ≥0.6 and raw-agreement≥0.8 before R5 adds the new asserted_capability_confirmed sub-answer.

Section-order permutation of plan text can flip the gate's final verdict (PASS↔BLOCK or PASS↔INDETERMINATE); E6 measures stability by running the full review_plan entrypoint over 14 permutable plans under 3 distinct section orderings and confirms κ≥0.6 and raw-agreement≥0.8 before R3 adds a new order-exposed container criterion.

Infrastructure-induced INDETERMINATE verdicts (LLM unavailable, verifier exhausted budget) must be excluded from agreement metrics and re-run rather than counted as stable judge outcomes; E6 operationalizes this by checking coverage.llm_unavailable and coverage.verify_failed flags.

The frozen E6 inputs (e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl and e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl) enable reproducible re-runs without live-store or LLM-corpus dependencies; section-order permutations are deterministically generated via seeded shuffle and committed to run files.

E6 produces bounded, honest LLM spend: 150 agentic Pass-2 calls (Exp A) plus 42 full-gate runs (Exp B); self-consistency and order-shuffle are inherently re-run measurements and cannot be read from persisted sidecars.

Self-consistency pass (κ≥0.6 and raw-agreement≥0.8) gates R5 landing; order-shuffle pass gates R3 landing; sub-floor results block their respective stories and are recorded verbatim in e6_summary.json.
